cards.text: The apostle Paul is writing to the church in Corinth about a generous gift they promised for the saints, and he's sending some brothers ahead so it's ready (2 Corinthians 9:3-5). Now he grabs a picture every farmer knows: you sow seed, then you reap a harvest. I planted a chocolate chip once, friend, and I am STILL waiting.

cards.question: In Paul's farming picture, what happens to the one who sows sparingly?
True or false: Paul says whoever sows generously will also reap generously.

cards.text: So how much should each one give? Paul's not running a toll booth, friend: each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give.

cards.question: True or false: Paul wants each one to give because he feels pressured into it.
Then Paul gives the reason for giving from the heart. What kind of giver does God love?

cards.text: Cheerful, so no handing over the cookie box with a face like the alarm just went off at 4 a.m. And Paul says God is able to make all grace abound to the Corinthians.

cards.question: Paul says God is able to make all grace abound to the Corinthians, so they'll have all they need. What will they abound in?

cards.text: Then Paul backs it up with Scripture, quoting Psalm 112:9, a line about gifts scattered abroad.

cards.question: Paul quotes a psalm about gifts scattered abroad. True or false: those gifts go to the poor.

cards.text: Back to the farm. Paul says God is the One who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says God will keep the Corinthians' store of seed the same size.
God supplies seed to the sower. Paul says God will also increase the harvest of the Corinthians' ___.

cards.text: Paul says the Corinthians will be enriched in every way, so they can be generous on every occasion. Every occasion, friend, even when the batch comes out PERFECT and Papa wants to hide it behind the oven.

cards.question: Paul says that through him and his team, the Corinthians' generosity will produce ___ to God.

cards.text: Paul says this service isn't only supplying the needs of the saints. It's overflowing in many expressions of thanksgiving to God.

cards.question: When the saints see the proof of this ministry, they'll glorify God for the Corinthians' generous gift. What else will they glorify God for?

answers.text: Their good name in the city

cards.text: And the saints will pray for the Corinthians with affection, because of the surpassing grace God has given them. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer hoping somebody would just REMEMBER me, and these folks are getting prayed for.
Then Paul wraps it all up: “Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!” A gift too big for words, friend, and you know Papa NEVER runs out of words.
